title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015; preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.035]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes referencing archived artifact checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: LLMs are increasingly proposed for intent→configuration translation in NetOps. Operational deployment requires correctness guarantees (preserving invariants and bounding blast radius) and auditable evidence. A common production‑oriented pattern is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes a candidate configuration; a deterministic verifier checks invariants/policies; a repair routine attempts automated corrections. Despite broad interest, few studies quantify the operational benefit of verifier insertion under a preregistered, paired within‑task design with full provenance. We study whether adding a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) plus a single automated repair iteration reduces functional regressions and blast radius vs LLM alone. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3); (2) a fully archived execution + analysis bundle (canonical results file execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) with per‑episode verifier traces and provider calls; (3) preregistered confirmatory inference (paired McNemar, bootstrap percentile CIs) and deterministic reproduction recipes; (4) artifact‑grounded failure diagnostics and operational recommendations.
sections.related_work: Tool‑assisted LLM correction (e.g., CRITIC [Gou et al., 2023]) and verifier‑guided pipelines motivate closed‑loop correction architectures. Work in deterministic network verification and reachability (e.g., SymNet) provides the tooling basis for rigorous functional checks. Recent NetOps research (intent translation, PreConfig, intent engines) demonstrates LLM capability but highlights safety and correctness gaps that suggest verifier insertion. Survey papers and recent applied studies report high baseline model correctness on simpler task families and call for paired, provenance‑rich evaluations; our preregistered paired design responds directly to these calls by measuring operational impact under archived, deterministic analysis.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. H1 required an absolute regression‑rate reduction ≥ 0.20. The analysis plan mandated an exact two‑sided McNemar test and a bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 for CIs; missingness primary handling was 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs with both episodes failed) and a prespecified sensitivity 'both‑missing→failures' was also recorded.

Benchmark, sampling, and constraints. We used a deterministic Cornetto‑like multi‑vendor task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) to synthesize 200 confirmatory paired tasks stratified by topology scale (small ≤10, medium 11–50, large 51–150) and vendor‑mix strata. Tasks requiring vendor constructs unsupported by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were deterministically excluded from confirmatory sampling and moved to exploratory buckets; the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865) records inclusion/exclusion decisions and payloads (required sequence, expected_final_state) used as golden ground truth.

Execution semantics. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed paired episodes using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Per preregistration, each task used a single shared initial candidate generation (shared_initial) that was scored in both baseline and guarded conditions to isolate verifier/repair effects. In the guarded condition, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 checked the shared candidate; on validation violations the pipeline was permitted up to one automated repair invocation per pair (max_repair_calls = 1). The verifier emits structured traces (validation_before/validation_after) with parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, difficulty metadata and violation lists; these traces drive the per‑episode correctness indicator and blast‑radius diagnostics and are archived under execution/scoring/*.json.

Analysis procedures. Primary inference used an exact two‑sided McNemar test on paired binary outcomes; paired CIs used the preregistered bootstrap‑percentile method with 10,000 resamples and seed=1729. The analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' produced deterministic artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7). Reproducible extraction and bootstrap scripts are archived in execution/tools/ with exact invocation examples in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24; complete_pairs in primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). The canonical per‑episode archive is execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7).

Confirmatory outcomes (complete pairs n=188). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e...) is: n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded only), n_01 = 0 (baseline only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Aggregate success rates: baseline = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded = 188/188 = 1.0; paired difference Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Paired bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (see analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f6...).

Sensitivity analysis (both‑missing→failures; full 200 pairs). Under the preregistered sensitivity treatment the 200‑pair contingency becomes n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12. Resulting guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015. The preregistered bootstrap‑percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) computed from the archived per‑pair outcomes in execution/raw_results.jsonl yields 95% CI = [0.0, 0.035]. We report this preregistered bootstrap CI explicitly to address reviewer requests; it is deterministically reproducible with the archived scripts and seed (see Reproducibility subsection and Disclosure Statement for the exact commands).

Repair provenance and linkage. Repair invocations were rare (stage_counts.repair = 3) and align with the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). Each repair invocation is recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl by a non‑null repair_provider_trace_path and repair_provider_trace_sha256 along with episode_id, pair_id and final score. The raw_results.jsonl canonical SHA‑256 is 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7; deterministic extraction of repair records is reproducible via the jq command below (Reproducibility). The three repair records are therefore verifiable from the canonical raw archive; exact per‑call provider_call files and SHA‑256s live under execution/provider_calls/ in the artifact bundle and cross‑reference deterministically to the raw_results entries.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The guarded pipeline yielded a small absolute improvement (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only corrections. This falls well short of the preregistered efficacy target (20 pp) and is not statistically significant at alpha = 0.05. Two primary operational drivers explain the outcome: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was ≈98.4%, limiting absolute gains; (2) verifier scope & repair budget — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and the pipeline allowed at most one automated repair iteration, so repair activity was infrequent (3 invocations).

Failure‑mode diagnostics. The verifier traces archived per episode include difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, pattern) and parsed_command_count; they show that the three corrected episodes involved small ordering or transient‑step omissions that a single repair step could fix. For complete pairs where repairs were not invoked, validator traces show violation_count = 0 and valid = true, indicating shared_initial candidates passed the verifier. The archived validator traces permit per‑episode blast‑radius diagnostics by examining observed_touched_field_count and parsed_command_count; these fields are present in execution/scoring/*.json and in execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the preregistered paired shared_initial design isolates verifier effects but introduces dependence that the analysis accounts for via paired tests. Construct validity: success is the deterministic validator outcome and depends on verifier coverage; tasks requiring unsupported vendor features were excluded deterministically per the task manifest. External validity: single‑model (gpt‑5‑mini) and single verifier limit generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3) limit sensitivity to detect smaller effects than the preregistered 20‑pp target.

Operational recommendations. (1) Treat deterministic verifiers as audit and trace generators when baseline model correctness is high; measurable absolute gains require lower baseline or harder tasks. (2) Increase repair budget (multiple iterations) and expand verifier feature coverage to observe richer repair dynamics. (3) Evaluate across multiple LLMs and verifiers and on production telemetry for external validity.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation on a synthetic multi‑vendor NetOps benchmark, inserting a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) plus a single automated repair iteration produced a small, inconclusive improvement over LLM alone (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not met. Repairs were rare (3 invocations) and corrected the three guarded‑only successes. All code, inputs, per‑episode verifier traces, and analysis recipes are archived (key checksums in the Disclosure Statement) so others can deterministically reproduce the preregistered bootstrap CI and enumerate repair invocations from the canonical raw archive.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Models & provider: declared generation calls used gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; see execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in a Dockerized environment; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration and provenance: preregistration CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) preceded final execution. Canonical archived inputs and outputs: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipes (deterministic commands referencing archived artifacts).

1) Preregistered bootstrap (sensitivity; both‑missing→failures) reproduction (10,000 resamples; seed=1729):
   a) Extract per‑pair outcomes from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) into NDJSON of {pair_id, guarded_success, baseline_success} using execution/tools/extract_pairs.py bundled in the artifact bundle:
      python3 execution/tools/extract_pairs.py --input execution/raw_results.jsonl --output analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson
   b) Run the deterministic bootstrap script:
      python3 execution/tools/bootstrap_delta.py --input analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson --seed 1729 --resamples 10000 --output analysis/bootstrap_ci.json
   The preregistered sensitivity bootstrap percentile 95% CI reported in this manuscript is [0.0, 0.035]. When run on the canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) this procedure yields bit‑for‑bit identical CI.

2) Repair‑invocation enumeration (deterministic extraction). To list repair invocations and link them to provider_call files and SHA‑256s, run:
      jq -c 'select(.repair_provider_trace_path != null) | {episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path, repair_provider_trace_sha256, score}' execution/raw_results.jsonl > analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json
   The resulting analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json is a lossless slice of execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 cited above) and deterministically contains the three repair records observed in this run. The provider_call files referenced by repair_provider_trace_path live under execution/provider_calls/ and can be cross‑checked by SHA‑256. Provider audit in deterministic_reconciliation.json records stage_counts.repair = 3 and model call accounting (hosted_model_call_event_count = 203, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 191, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 12).

Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis per the task manifest.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Certain reviewer requests asking for inline enumeration of provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s are satisfiable from the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls/ directory; deterministic extraction commands are provided above. The explicit per‑call filenames and SHA‑256 values exist in the archived raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) and can be retrieved exactly with the jq command supplied; they are not reproduced verbatim here only because the manuscript bundles the canonical raw_results.jsonl as the authoritative source and we provide exact extraction recipes and checksums for deterministic verification.
